data.label: Synthetic user
data.description: Synthetic test person who chats through a browser. External caller, not provisioned.

data.label: Sign-in
data.description: Authenticates synthetic users (OIDC) and issues tokens. The app validates them before any chat turn. Anonymous access is denied.

data.label: Assistant app
data.description: Chat web app and API. It validates the App ID token, loads and saves per-user state, applies the context bound, calls the model, returns the answer and triggers escalation. It takes no external actions.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Per-user conversation documents, partitioned by user ID. A user can only read their own partition through the app.

data.label: Context bounder
data.description: Requested conceptual step owned by the assistant app. It caps history turns and tokens and screens input before the model call. Not a separate deployment.
data.service: Logic in the IBM Cloud Code Engine app

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Foundation model inference. The model, plan, region availability and quotas still need to be chosen and verified. Local tests use a scripted mock instead.

data.label: Escalation
data.description: Sends a handoff notice with a conversation reference when the user asks for a person or the app abstains.

data.label: Human support
data.description: Person or queue that receives escalations. External to the provisioning scope.

data.label: Logs & audit
data.description: Application logs, latency, errors and escalation audit, with no raw chat content by default.

brief.application: Use IBM Cloud for this synthetic architecture qualification. Build an authenticated conversational assistant for synthetic users. Include an application, per-user conversation state, model runtime, bounded context and an escalation path. No external actions in this first test. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: What information will it work with, and where does it live?
lastAsked.beginner: For example a database, documents, or another system's data.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the AI architecture design.

requirements.statement: Proposed: only signed-in users can chat, and each user can read only their own conversation history.
requirements.rationale: If one user's history is shown to another user, that is a privacy breach. Unauthenticated access would bypass audit.
requirements.basis: "Build an authenticated conversational assistant" with "per-user conversation state"

requirements.statement: Proposed: each model call includes only a bounded amount of that user's recent history. The limit is still to be agreed.
requirements.rationale: Unbounded context raises cost and latency and can exceed the model's limits.

requirements.statement: Proposed: the user can request a person, and the app escalates when it cannot answer. Escalations are recorded, and no external actions are taken.
requirements.rationale: Without escalation, users get stuck with wrong or empty answers.
requirements.basis: "an escalation path. No external actions in this first test."

decisions.subject: design.ibm-authenticated-conversational-assistant-first-sketch
decisions.title: IBM authenticated conversational assistant (first sketch)
decisions.context: End-to-end sketch: synthetic user → App ID sign-in → Code Engine assistant app → Cloudant per-user state, context bounding, watsonx.ai model, escalation through Event Notifications to a human queue, with logs in IBM Cloud Logs. No external actions. Assumptions: region to be selected; model choice, plan, quotas and IBM account access are unverified; there is no native generator for this workload yet, so engineering is required.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
